serbia.title: Flag of the Republic of Serbia

colors.note: One of the traditional pan-Slavic colours, symbolising blood shed for freedom.
The second pan-Slavic colour, representing freedom and loyalty.
The double-headed eagle and crown of the lesser coat of arms, reflecting royal Serbian tradition.

desc:
- Three equal horizontal bands of red, blue, and white (pan-Slavic colours) with the lesser coat of arms set to the hoist side
- The coat of arms shows a white double-headed eagle with the Serbian Cross on a red shield, topped by a royal crown
- The modern form was codified on 11 November 2010 during the Republic of Serbia's post-Yugoslav era
trivia:
- The red-blue-white tricolour dates back to 1835, introduced under Prince Milos Obrenovic
- The Serbian Cross — a cross with four stylised 'C' letters — is said to stand for 'Samo sloga Srbina spasava' ('Only unity saves the Serbs')
- Serbia uses both a state flag (with coat of arms) and a simpler civil flag (without)
